found_while: 2026-11-11: building the Time Machine (gaps it shows around 1250)

items.name: Yuan Dynasty
items.why: China jumps from the Song (ends 1279) to the Ming (1368): the Mongol Yuan dynasty under Kublai Khan is missing.

items.name: Mongols Sack Baghdad
items.why: Would 'end' the Abbasid Caliphate and the Islamic Golden Age, which both stop in 1258 with nothing to end them.

items.name: Mamluk Sultanate
items.why: Egypt and Syria's rulers for 250 years (they stopped the Mongols at Ain Jalut) have no span.

items.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
items.why: Saladin's dynasty, central to the Crusades, has no span.

items.name: Fatimid Caliphate
items.why: The caliphate that founded Cairo has no span; the Middle East lane is thin before the Crusades.

items.name: Seljuk Empire
items.why: Its victory at Manzikert helped set off the Crusades.

items.name: Ilkhanate
items.why: The Mongol state in Persia that sacked Baghdad.

items.name: Golden Horde
items.why: The Mongol state that ruled the Russian principalities for two centuries.

items.name: Kievan Rus'
items.why: Exists only as its founding event; the state itself, ended by the Mongol invasion, has no span.

items.name: Kamakura Shogunate
items.why: Japan has nothing between ancient times and the Tokugawa; the first shogunate (which repelled the Mongol invasions) is missing.

items.name: Heian Period
items.why: Classical Japan (The Tale of Genji) has no span.

items.name: Khmer Empire
items.why: The builders of Angkor; Southeast Asia has almost nothing before 1500.

items.name: Srivijaya
items.why: The maritime trading empire of Sumatra, a major Buddhist centre; Southeast Asia is thin.

items.name: Ghana Empire
items.why: West Africa's first great empire, before Mali; Africa before 1500 is thin.

items.name: Kingdom of Kongo
items.why: Central Africa's major kingdom, in contact with Portugal from the 1480s, has no span.
